note: THE DEFECT, as distinct from the reported wording (see match-silent.json for that). Present when the uninitialised accumulator survives into the emitted DXIL as an undef-seeded `phi float` AND the module is nonetheless accepted -- no error, so DXIL validation passed. That pair is the whole complaint: the identical read written straight-line IS rejected (`error: Instructions should not read uninitialized value.`), so the loop spelling is the compiler declining to diagnose what it diagnoses elsewhere. CONTROLS: control-initialized.hlsl is the same shader with `result = 0.0;` added -- one line different, correct code -- and must NOT match (`--expect no-match`); it emits `phi float [ %10, %5 ], [ 0.000000e+00, %4 ]`, the same phi with a constant instead of undef. variant-straightline.hlsl (the reporter's own commented-out line) must also NOT match, because it errors. NARROWNESS IS DELIBERATE: a predicate matching `undef` anywhere in DXIL fires on correct shaders, because several DXIL ops carry structurally-undef operands in valid code -- `loadInput`'s trailing gsVertexAxis operand is `undef` in every non-GS shader and is right there in the reporter's own paste, and unused coordinate operands are undef too. Matching `undef` reaching an arithmetic *dx.op* would not work either: here the arithmetic is a plain LLVM `fadd`, not a dx.op call. ANCHORING: the phi clause is positive, so a compile that never emitted DXIL cannot satisfy this predicate -- which is what stops the `not_regex error:` absence clause from being satisfied for free by a release that failed to parse the shader. The `error:` clause also protects against the validator quoting the instruction it rejects back into its own diagnostic (`note: at '...' in block ...`), which would otherwise let a rejected module match the phi clause. LIMITATION: it does not check that the undef reaches an fadd, so a future codegen that emitted a dead undef phi would score as a repro.
